title: Microburst response presets and cost estimate
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note collects a compact set of recommended presets and a back-of-envelope cost estimate for microburst-heavy, session-oriented chat workloads (mobile app notifications, customer support quick-replies, search-autocomplete with short completions). The intent is a lightweight, actionable starting point teams can drop into route configs and then A/B with live traffic.

Summary recommendations (one-line):
- Batching: favour micro-batches with adaptive batching windows (target per-GPU batch 4–12 tokens/requests depending on size).
- Cache: short TTL prefix/KV caching tuned to session heartbeat (15–45s) with route-aware bypass for context-sensitive routes.
- Quantization: default to 4-bit dynamic quant for ~7B-class models; keep 8-bit fallback for routes with high hallucination risk.
- Warmup: maintain small warm pool for endpoints expected to see sub-5s bursts (pool size = concurrent_burst_peak * 0.2).

Why microbursts are different:
- High concurrency, low per-request token counts, and short-lived peaks make naive large-batch optimizations ineffective. Large batching increases tail latency which kills user experience for interactive flows.
- Cost win comes mostly from avoiding repeated forward passes of repeated context (prefixs), and from opportunistic small batching that pushes compute utilization without adding latency.

Detailed presets and rationale:
1) Workload classes (for mapping presets):
- session-signal (short chat messages, 4–40 tokens generated)
- autocomplete (very short completions, 1–12 tokens)
- transactional-summarize (100–300 token outputs but rare; treat as separate route)

2) Batching presets:
- session-signal: target_batch_size_gpu = 6 requests; max_microbatch_wait = 8ms; grouping by payload-length-buckets (0–32, 33–128). Rationale: small waits avoid noticeable latency while still enabling some kernel-level batching.
- autocomplete: target_batch_size_gpu = 12 requests; max_microbatch_wait = 6ms; prefer HW-accelerated gather kernels where available.
- transactional-summarize: batch aggressively off-peak (target 32+), but on microburst windows fall back to immediate scheduling to keep latency bounded.

Implementation notes: prioritize continuous batching where we allow an initial low wait to accumulate across a few concurrent requests rather than fixed global batch sizes. Use request grouping by length and model-compatibility tag to avoid padding overhead.

3) Cache presets (KV and prefix caching):
- session-signal: prefix_KV_TTL = 30s; prefix_KV_hashing = session_id + last_user_turn_hash; allow 1k prefix entries per GPU shard before eviction (LRU).
- autocomplete: prefix_KV_TTL = 15s; aggressive reuse by keying on prefix tokens and client-region.
- transactional-summarize: caching disabled by default unless identical doc fingerprints are detected.

Rationales: TTLs tuned to session heartbeat behavior observed in beta customers: many mobile clients send repeated short turns within 10–40s windows. Short TTLs capture those without causing cache pollution. Hash on last_user_turn reduces false hits when context changed.

4) Quantization (qconfig) presets:
- default model class 7B-decoder (non-instruction-tuned): use dynamic 4-bit (nf4/awq style) with mixed-precision activation; expected quality delta ~0.5–1% on internal n-gram overlap tests.
- critical routes (high factuality need): force 8-bit quant (or FP16) as fallback; use route tag `quality:high` to pin.
- large models (>=13B): prefer 8-bit quant with block-wise quantization to preserve accuracy; reserve 4-bit for non-critical analytics jobs.

Operational notes: expose per-route qconfig in the routing table so rollouts can test lower precision on internal canaries first. Monitor perplexity and hallucination signals in real-time and auto-revert plan if quality regressions exceed thresholds.

5) Warm pools and pre-warm strategy:
- For routes expecting microbursts: pre-warm ratio = ceil(peak_concurrency * 0.2). Example: expected peak 100 concurrent -> warm pool 20 containers/GPU slots.
- Warm retention: 60s after last observed burst before recycling.

Cost model (back-of-envelope):
Assumptions: 7B model, 1M requests where each request generates 20 tokens on average, baseline FP16 token cost (hosted) = $0.35 per 1k tokens (example), 4-bit quant reduces inference cost by ~30–45% depending on kernel stack, batching raises token throughput by ~1.5x for micro-batching.
Scenarios (per 1M requests, 20 tokens per request => 20M tokens):
- baseline FP16, no cache: raw token units = 20M => cost ~= 20M/1000 * $0.35 = $7,000.
- microbatch + prefix cache (30s) + 4-bit quant: token cost reduction factors: quant ~0.6, batching efficiency ~0.67 effective cost, caching hit rate conservative 18% (saves duplicate token expands). Effective cost ~= $7,000 * 0.6 * 0.67 * 0.82 = ~$2,300 (order-of-magnitude).
Notes: these are illustrative; linked spreadsheet contains per-route detailed rows and sensitivity sweeps.

Sensitivity and recommended experiments (priority order):
1) Run 72-hour A/B on one customer route toggling 4-bit vs 8-bit with live eval hooks (ROUGE, hallucination markers).
2) Sweep prefix_KV_TTL across 10/20/30/60s with traffic replay to measure hit-rate and cache churn cost.
3) Microbatch wait sweep (2/6/10ms) measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and cost per token.
4) Test warm-pool sizing with synthetic bursts to measure cold-start miss rate and service degradation.

Spreadsheet columns (what I used in linked sheet): route, workload_class, avg_request_tokens, avg_generated_tokens, expected_peak_concurrency, baseline_cost_per_1k, qconfig_setting, batch_preset, cache_TTL, estimated_hit_rate, estimated_cost_1M_requests, notes. Keep these columns to reproduce the model quickly.

Next steps / owner actions:
- (Nikhil) schedule A/B with Solutions Eng on customer 'Nomad Chat' for session-signal route (start week of 2025-11-17).
- (Ava) add quick telemetry hooks for hallucination proxy metrics to the route-level dashboard.
- (Marcus) prototype adaptive microbatcher improvements to allow dynamic max_wait adjustment based on live p50 latency.

Open questions and risks:
- Stability of 4-bit kernels across model revisions (needs ongoing benching).
- Cache privacy concerns for multi-tenant private deployments — need to ensure keys honor tenant isolation.
- Edge cases where small batching interacts poorly with token streaming; verify streaming semantics with microbatching enabled.

Appendix: quick checklist for adoption:
- Add route tags: workload_class, q_sensitivity, expected_burst_window
- Plug recommended presets into per-route config templates (examples included in spreadsheet)
- Run the experiment plan and collect cost + quality telemetry for 2 weeks before wide rollout.

Notes: this is a working drafting memo. The spreadsheet linked above contains the numeric sweeps and per-route row-level estimates. Feedback welcome — if you have live traces I can plug them into the sensitivity sheet and return a more precise sizing and expected savings projection.
